previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic steroid-dependent asthma, and CMV gastritis was admitted for an acute asthma exacerbation and worsening epigastric pain following a recent alcohol binge. He was treated with BiPAP, intravenous steroids, and nebulizers, with gradual improvement in respiratory status. His abdominal pain was attributed to a flare of CMV gastritis, and he was restarted on valganciclovir. Alcohol withdrawal was monitored with CIWA, though symptoms were mild. He was discharged on a prednisone taper, atovaquone for PCP prophylaxis, and continued valganciclovir. Follow-up was arranged with pulmonology, sleep medicine, and hepatology for ongoing management of asthma, possible sleep apnea, and a liver nodule noted on prior imaging. He committed to sobriety and medication adherence.
problems: Other specified gastritis, without mention of hemorrhage

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ with a PMHx of asthma, alcohol 
cirrhosis who presented with asthma exacerbation and alcohol 
withdrawal, who was found to have elevated beta glucan levels, 
pulmonary nodules on CT, and esophageal candidiasis. 

Patient was started on high dose steroids for asthma 
exacerbation and was discharged on taper. He also treated with 
course of ceftriaxone/azithromycin for possible CAP. Given 
chronic steroid use, he was also started on bactrim 1 SS tap 
daily for PCP prophylaxis, cal/vitD, and PPI. He underwent 
___ biopsy of a pulmonary nodule. Preliminary studies were 
significant for negative gram stain, no fungal organisms on ___ 
prep, negative AFB smear and negative PJP. Biopsy was consistent 
with scar tissue.

Patient underwent EGD during hospitalization which was negative 
for varices but did show esophageal candidiasis for which he was 
started on fluconazole. Gastric biopsy showed gastropathy. He 
was due for surveillance MRCP given dysplastic nodules which was 
repeated during hospitalization and showed no evidence of HCC.

Brief hospital course:

#respiratory distress/nodular opacities: Patient presented with 
acute respiratory distress and hypoxia requiring ___ NC. His 
respiratory distress was felt to be primarily due to severe 
asthma exacerbation. His respiratory status improved with high 
dose steroids and scheduled nebulizers. Flu negative. He was 
also treated with a 7 day course of antibiotics with 
azithromycin and CTX for possible CAP. PCP was also on 
differential given prolonged steroid use and elevated beta 
glucan (which was checked to rule out infiltrative liver disease 
given elevated alk phos, see below). Patient also had 
significant chest pain. EKG had no ST segment changes and he had 
negative tropoinins. CTA was performed to rule out PE given 
chest pain and hypoxia. CTA was negative for PE but showed 
several nodular opacities. Given presence of nodules on CT in 
context of elevated beta glucan, ID and pulmonology were 
consulted. Workup included urinary histoplasmosis, galactomannam 
and coccidiodes antibody, which were negative. Patient underwent 
___ guided biopsy of nodular opacities which, histology of which 
was consistent with scar formation. Bronchoscopy was deferred 
given severity of asthma exacerbation. Respiratory distress and 
hypoxia gradually improved with steroids and nebulizers. TTE 
showed mild pulmonary hypertension. Repeat beta glucan was 
normal. Patient was discharged on prolonged steroid taper with 
pulmonary follow up. 

# Alcohol withdrawal: Patient presented with EtOH level of 369, 
about 24 hours after last reported drink. He was showing signs 
of alcohol withdrawal including tremulousness, tachycardia, 
hypertension and diffuse abdominal pain. He was maintained on 
CIWA protocol q3h with ativan for CIWA >10. He was also started 
on PO thiamine and folate. 

#esophageal candidiasis: Patient underwent EGD during hospital 
course. Last EGD was in ___ and patient had not followed up 
for repeat EGD 8 weeks later to ensure resolution of gastric 
ulcers. EGD this hospitalization showed gastropathy and 
esophageal candidiasis. He was started on 14 day course of 
fluconazole and continued on BID PPI. 

# Alcoholic cirrhosis complicated by alc hep on presentation: 
MELD score 11, Childs A on admission. DF 6. Abdominal ultrasound 
on admission without ascites. He presented with 2:1 AST:ALT 
elevation and all phos elevated greater than baseline. In 
addition to alcoholic hepatitis, this also raised concern for 
infiltrative disease for which fungal markers and quant-gold 
were sent, which were negative as above. LFTs downtrended during 
hospitalization. Previous MR in ___ showed dysplastic 
nodules, for which follow up in 3 months was recommended. MRCP 
was repeated which showed no lesions concerning for HCC. EGD 
this admission with no varices.

#pancytopenia: patient had downtrending H/H, WBC. Platelets 
stable. Presentation was felt to be due to BM suppression 
secondary to liver disease and/or acute illness. GIB secondary 
to gastritis also on differential, however EGD ruled out frank 
bleeding. Differential on ___ showed more immature cell lines. 
Retic count elevated.

#ongoing primary care: patient states that he can no longer see 
his prior PCP and would like to see a provider through whom he 
can also be on suboxone. Phone number was provided for HCA. 
Patient was also encouraged to follow up with pulm/hepatology at 
___.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ trainee and Dr. ___ radiologist.

TECHNIQUE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient.  After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained.  A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a LPO position on the CT scan table.  Limited
preprocedure CTscan of the intended biopsy area was performed.  Based on the
